topic: Close the full two-nuisance structure-agnostic minimax gap for the partially linear causal coefficient: match Gu–Yin–Cai–Fan Appendix A.1 with a budget-aware two-sided empirical-balancing estimator, or prove the missing cross-stochastic lower bound

open_problems.open_problem: Is the missing cross-stochastic interaction in Gu–Yin–Cai–Fan's four-budget partially linear model minimax unavoidable over all estimators, rather than only over black-box-oracle or first-order estimator classes?

source_refs.claim: Appendix A.1 defines the full two-nuisance risk, gives nonmatching upper and lower bounds, and presents the result as a starting point for future study.
source_refs.author: Yihong Gu, Qishuo Yin, Tianxi Cai, Jianqing Fan

source_refs.claim: The COLT open-problem note identifies variance propagation as the feature missed by earlier structure-agnostic lower bounds for the partially linear coefficient.
source_refs.author: Yihong Gu

source_refs.excerpt: define whether the converse ranges over arbitrary estimators ... or over black-box-oracle estimators
Sudakov/Haar lower-bound witness, and two-point minimax testing-distance argument are the open mathematical steps.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Appendix A.1's hard classes do not reproduce every interaction among the two stochastic budgets and two approximation budgets. The prior CausalSmith reviews expose an additional quantifier problem: marginal nuisance-rate budgets can define an oracle experiment, a restricted estimator class, or a full statistical model, and a lower bound for one need not hold for the others. No cited construction jointly perturbs both nuisances, preserves the partially linear law and all four budgets, keeps testing distance small, and shifts the coefficient at the proposed cross-stochastic scale.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A minimax lower-bound theorem over an explicitly defined all-estimator experiment, with a finite-support Le Cam or fuzzy-hypothesis family producing the cross-stochastic separation in every claimed budget regime, or a counterexample showing that marginal budgets alone cannot imply that term.

writing_exemplar.why: Its budget decomposition and Appendix A.1 lead directly from the solved one-sided model to the unresolved two-nuisance converse.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: separate nuisance approximation from stochastic error -> solve the one-learnable-nuisance minimax problem -> allow both nuisances to carry four independent budgets -> determine whether the cross-stochastic term is unavoidable

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the fuzzy-hypothesis and sequential-perturbation lower-bound proof, with asymmetric perturbation order chosen to isolate a genuinely cross-stochastic separation.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It proves sharp mixed-bias and squared-nuisance lower bounds from black-box tolerances, the nearest existing machinery to the required four-budget converse.

method_exemplars.technique: Carry over the variance-propagation hard-instance decomposition and strengthen its testing construction to two random nuisance channels.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It isolates the same partially linear target and identifies stochastic variance propagation as the obstruction that older lower bounds omit.

open_problems.open_problem: Can a budget-aware two-sided empirical-balancing estimator attain one explicit full two-nuisance risk bound without assuming away the fold-conditional cross-stochastic empirical-process remainder?

source_refs.claim: Appendix A.1 upper-bounds the full problem by an oracle choice between one-sided SADE and DML rather than by a single two-sided attaining estimator.
source_refs.author: Yihong Gu, Qishuo Yin, Tianxi Cai, Jianqing Fan

source_refs.claim: Augmented minimax-linear estimation chooses weights through an empirical worst-case bias and variance criterion and proves asymptotic efficiency under weak conditions.
source_refs.author: David A. Hirshberg, Stefan Wager

source_refs.excerpt: Conjecture 1 still needs the empirical-process step for triangular-array local weights and cross-fit nuisance learners.
triangular-array empirical-process control for cross-fit localized DR scores is conjectural

open_problems.why_unsolved: Population orthogonality controls deterministic mixed bias but not the fold-conditional random term created when both learned nuisances enter the same balanced score. Gu et al.'s one-sided calibration squares one stochastic radius, while Appendix A.1 falls back to an oracle minimum with DML; the adjacent prior proposal likewise lacked a maximal inequality uniform over learner outputs and triangular-array weights. A two-sided program must balance two random error classes without paying weight variance or dependence large enough to erase the cross-stochastic gain.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An oracle inequality for an explicit cross-fitted two-sided balancing program, including a fold-conditional empirical-process bound and a risk rate stated in all four nuisance budgets, with matching asymptotic or finite-sample variance control.

writing_exemplar.why: It supplies the exact one-sided balancing construction and ends with the two-sided upper-bound gap that the new estimator must fill.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: DML pays a product of total nuisance errors -> one-sided empirical balancing removes first-order stochastic error -> both nuisance learners may be noisy and misspecified -> build one two-sided estimator that attains the four-budget rate

method_exemplars.technique: Extend the adversarial empirical-balancing weight program and localized-Rademacher oracle proof to simultaneous calibration against both nuisance error classes.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its one-sided SADE construction already squares one nuisance's stochastic radius in the identical partially linear model.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt augmented minimax-linear weights, worst-case bias and variance duality, and the conditional asymptotic-linearity proof.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired object is a balancing rule whose observable objective must trade two imbalance channels against weight variance.

method_exemplars.technique: Use foldwise conditioning and the exact orthogonal-score expansion to isolate population drift, score noise, and nuisance-replacement leakage before applying the new maximal inequality.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It gives the canonical cross-fit decomposition for the same partially linear causal coefficient.

open_problems.open_problem: Can one estimator adapt to unknown outcome- and treatment-nuisance approximation and stochastic budgets while attaining the oracle minimum of the SADE and DML two-nuisance rates?

source_refs.claim: Appendix A.1's combined upper bound assumes knowledge of both nuisance budget vectors, while the paper's budget-agnostic remark covers only a fixed outcome learner in the one-sided setting.
source_refs.author: Yihong Gu, Qishuo Yin, Tianxi Cai, Jianqing Fan

source_refs.claim: Augmented minimax-linear weights provide an observable empirical bias and variance optimization, but do not establish adaptation over the four structure-agnostic nuisance budgets.
source_refs.author: David A. Hirshberg, Stefan Wager

open_problems.why_unsolved: The Appendix A.1 selector uses unobserved budget vectors to decide whether SADE or DML has the smaller bound. Fixed-class tuning independence in the one-sided theorem does not select among two learner families or their complexity levels. Estimating local critical radii and approximation errors on the same data introduces selection dependence, so a naive plug-in rule can lose precisely the cross-stochastic improvement it seeks to preserve.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A data-driven selector or aggregated balancing estimator with a uniform oracle inequality over a grid of two-nuisance learner classes, plus a matching adaptation lower bound if the oracle minimum cannot be attained without a penalty.

writing_exemplar.why: Its Appendix makes the budget-known oracle comparison explicit, allowing a direct pivot from the full-risk bound to the adaptation problem.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: known budgets choose between SADE and DML -> users do not observe approximation or stochastic budgets -> data-driven selection can reintroduce stochastic error -> attain the oracle rate adaptively or quantify its price

method_exemplars.technique: Use the primal-dual minimax imbalance criterion as an observable risk proxy and port its conditional bias, variance, and central-limit analysis to learner aggregation.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It replaces unknown regression error directions by an empirical balancing objective rather than requiring population budgets.

method_exemplars.technique: Use nested sample splitting to separate learner and selector training from score evaluation, then prove a uniform orthogonal-score remainder bound.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Sample separation directly targets the dependence introduced by data-driven nuisance and estimator selection.

open_problems.open_problem: Can the full four-budget minimax rate for the partially linear causal coefficient be paired with honest confidence intervals that are uniformly valid across all two-nuisance regimes?

source_refs.claim: The one-sided SADE theorem obtains asymptotic normality only under additional conditions, whereas Appendix A.1 gives only nonmatching risk bounds in the full two-nuisance model.
source_refs.author: Yihong Gu, Qishuo Yin, Tianxi Cai, Jianqing Fan

source_refs.claim: DML gives cross-fitted asymptotic normality for the partially linear coefficient under a small product remainder, but does not target the sharper four-budget structure-agnostic frontier.
source_refs.author: Victor Chernozhukov, Denis Chetverikov, Mert Demirer, Esther Duflo, Christian Hansen, Whitney Newey, James Robins

open_problems.why_unsolved: Point-risk attainment does not imply coverage when the optimal bias is of sampling order and the active weighting rule changes with the nuisance budgets. Gu et al.'s one-sided efficient limit theorem imposes additional sup-norm and variance-learning conditions, while DML's expansion requires a negligible product remainder. Neither handles uniform coverage at the unresolved two-sided frontier or the nonregular switching among rate regimes.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A uniform asymptotic-linear or bias-aware limit theorem with a consistently estimable variance and an honest confidence interval whose radius matches the full minimax rate, or an impossibility theorem quantifying the unavoidable honesty or adaptation penalty.

writing_exemplar.why: It already separates sharp point estimation from efficient asymptotic normality and exposes the absence of the latter in Appendix A.1.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: one-sided balancing sharpens point estimation -> causal use requires uncertainty quantification -> the two-nuisance optimum switches regimes and may retain nonnegligible bias -> obtain honest minimax-rate inference

method_exemplars.technique: Port the cross-fitted influence-function expansion, foldwise variance estimator, and uniform Gaussian approximation while replacing the product remainder by calibrated-balance remainders.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the canonical inference proof for the identical partially linear causal coefficient.

method_exemplars.technique: Extend the variance-weighted SADE program and its conditional central-limit proof to two balancing directions and regime selection.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It already attains minimal asymptotic variance in the one-sided version of the target model.

open_problems.open_problem: How does the four-budget structure-agnostic minimax rate change when non-Gaussian treatment residuals permit higher-order orthogonality, including local-to-Gaussian cumulant regimes?

source_refs.claim: Appendix A.1 formulates the unresolved full frontier through four learner budgets but does not include a treatment-noise cumulant phase diagram.
source_refs.author: Yihong Gu, Qishuo Yin, Tianxi Cai, Jianqing Fan

source_refs.claim: For the partially linear model, DML is minimax under Gaussian treatment noise but can be suboptimal under independent non-Gaussian noise, where ACE uses the first nonzero higher cumulant.
source_refs.author: Jikai Jin, Lester Mackey, Vasilis Syrgkanis

source_refs.claim: Second-order orthogonal moments in partially linear regression exist if and only if the treatment residual is nonnormal.
source_refs.author: Lester Mackey, Vasilis Syrgkanis, Ilias Zadik
source_refs.venue: International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 80

open_problems.why_unsolved: The budget-based SADE analysis and cumulant-based ACE analysis exploit different mechanisms. ACE's robustness is indexed by the first usable treatment-noise cumulant, while Appendix A.1's unresolved terms arise from separate approximation and stochastic errors of two black-box learners. No cited result identifies which interactions remain minimax when both mechanisms coexist, especially near Gaussianity where cumulants shrink and estimating their usable order is itself noisy.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A minimax phase-diagram theorem indexed jointly by the four nuisance budgets and treatment cumulants, with an attaining cumulant-adaptive balancing or orthogonal estimator and matching lower bounds that include the Gaussian boundary.

writing_exemplar.why: Its framing converts the Gaussian versus non-Gaussian treatment-noise split into a precise minimax question in the same partially linear model.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: first-order DML is the default -> higher-order robustness is blocked by Gaussian noise but enabled by nonzero cumulants -> learner budgets create a separate two-nuisance frontier -> characterize the joint cumulant and budget phase diagram

method_exemplars.technique: Carry over the ACE moment construction, structure-agnostic cumulant estimation, and Gaussian versus non-Gaussian minimax testing arguments.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies both an attaining higher-order procedure and noise-sensitive lower bounds in the same model.

method_exemplars.technique: Use higher-order Neyman orthogonality and the Stein-lemma impossibility proof to identify feasible moment orders and the Gaussian boundary.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired phase diagram must reconcile empirical balancing with exactly this existence and nonexistence frontier.

method_exemplars.technique: Combine two-sided empirical calibration with the higher-order score and control localized empirical-process terms separately by each learner budget.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the nearest construction for removing stochastic learner error without imposing nuisance smoothness.

literature_map:
Robinson (1988, Econometrica, doi:10.2307/1912705) supplies the classical root-n partially linear residualization benchmark.
Chernozhukov et al. (2018, Econometrics Journal, doi:10.1111/ectj.12097; arXiv:1608.00060) establish cross-fitted DML and its product-of-nuisance-errors remainder for the PLM.
Mackey, Syrgkanis, and Zadik (2018, ICML, arXiv:1711.00342) show that higher-order orthogonality in the PLM exists exactly off the Gaussian treatment-residual boundary.
Athey, Imbens, and Wager (2018, JRSSB, doi:10.1111/rssb.12268; arXiv:1604.07125) give approximate residual balancing, a structure-aware predecessor for empirical balancing plus inference.
Hirshberg and Wager (2021, Annals of Statistics, doi:10.1214/21-AOS2080; arXiv:1712.00038) develop augmented minimax-linear weights and a bias-variance duality suited to balancing proofs.
Chernozhukov, Newey, and Singh (2022, Econometrica, doi:10.3982/ECTA18515; arXiv:1809.05224) automate Riesz-representer debiasing and inference for causal linear functionals.
Balakrishnan, Kennedy, and Wasserman (2023, arXiv:2305.04116) formalize structure-agnostic minimax lower bounds and explain why black-box first-order procedures can be optimal.
Jin and Syrgkanis (2024/2025, arXiv:2402.14264) prove structure-agnostic optimality of doubly robust ATE and ATT learning, but not the PLM four-budget variance frontier.
Bonvini, Kennedy, Dukes, and Balakrishnan (2024, arXiv:2405.08525) combine structure-agnostic nuisance classes with smoothness and obtain doubly robust inference under one inconsistent nuisance.
Gu (2025, COLT, PMLR 291) explicitly isolates variance propagation as the unresolved structure-agnostic PLM issue.
Jin, Mackey, and Syrgkanis (2025, arXiv:2507.02275) resolve Gaussian and noise-specific PLM cases and show that non-Gaussian ACE can beat DML.
Jin and Syrgkanis (2025/2026, arXiv:2512.17341) give sharp mixed-bias and squared-error lower bounds via sequential perturbations, a template for the missing cross-stochastic converse.
Gu, Yin, Cai, and Fan (2026, arXiv:2606.06368) prove SADE's one-sided rate and lower bound, but Appendix A.1 leaves the full two-nuisance bounds nonmatching and budget-aware.
Waagepetersen et al. (2026, arXiv:2607.03351) study outcome-adapted AutoDML efficiency, underscoring that representation and weight learning affect variance without resolving the full minimax ledger.
The live tension is sharp: one-sided SADE, DML, and noise-adaptive ACE dominate in different regimes, while no verified paper supplies one four-budget rate, an adaptive attaining estimator, matching cross-stochastic lower bounds, and uniform inference.
prior_proposal_map:
The exact qid stat_plm_two_nuisance_minimax/v1 has initialization records but no earlier proposal or review artifact.
The closest minimax source is banked stat_sa_cate_pointwise/v1; its §11 scope and angle0_v2 review expose the unresolved estimator-class quantifier and missing nuisance-product Le Cam pair.
That source also leaves the upper-side fold-conditional empirical-process argument open for cross-fitted two-nuisance learners.
The closest lower-bound-frontier source is eid_dml_orthogonality_frontier/v1, especially rejected angle 0 and reviewer rounds angle0_v1 through angle0_v5.
Those records separate population bilinear drift from empirical nuisance leakage and repeatedly demand a formal minimax or testing-distance quantifier.
Rejected angle 2 of the same qid was inspected for its augmented-balancing and Riesz connection; its unresolved step is CEINR admissibility from primitive moment equations.
Failed bank entry eid_dml_orth_uniform/v2 records that a proposed locally robust versus AutoDML separation was vacuous under its finite-support balancing space.
Adjacent eid_dml_orth_uniform/v1 and eid_dml_fold_spectrum_phase/v1 were inspected but not promoted because weak-overlap studentization and unequal-fold questions are less direct for this scalar minimax target.
